newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Thursday, led by gold, ending a three day recovery from a three week downtrend, with IMF gold sales plans remaining a market negative, traders said.

"The IMF has probably had the needed majority in favor of selling some gold for some time, but it may not happen for some time, and the real reason gold has been on the defensive is the lack of inflation and the relative attraction of stock and bond markets for investors," Paine Webber commodities research director Bernard Savaiko said.

IMF head Michel Camdessus said Thursday the IMF had the needed 85 percent majority in favor of the plan to sell about five million ounces of its 104 million ounce reserve to help fund third world debt relief, but U.S. Treasury Secretary Rubin said the sales may not be needed until the year 2000.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.70 an ounce at $383.60 an ounce, after falling to a fresh three year low at $382.60 an ounce early.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted around $381.10, after seeing a fresh three month low early at $379.80, testing a key support level that has held since early 1995.

"While nearby support continues to hold at $380, this market remains vulnerable to fresh short selling, which could take prices toward the longer term technical objective of $374," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
One month implied gold lease rates ended around 1.59 percent, after moving up sharply from around 1.33 early, after closing around 1.47 percent Wednesday.
"The rise in short lease rates suggests fresh shorts may be coming into the market," BV Capital Markets New York based analyst John Brimelow said.
COMEX December silver ended down 3.70 cents at $4.885 an ounce, after trading in a $4.930-4.875 range, with December silver remained above last Friday's low of $4.810.
The gold/silver ratio has come off its 78.55 highs seen last Friday, ending at 78.25 Thursday, as gold led the complex lower.

NYMEX October platinum ended down $2.20 an ounce at $387.90, after seeing a new low for the October contract at $386.50 intraday, with spot platinum fixing at $385.25 in London Thursday, its lowest level since January 31, 1994.
NYMEX December palladium ended down $1.45 at $119.00.
